# PiTTy v0.6.1 — tabs that stay in sync

v0.6.0 introduced independent conversations, but it also left several parts of the interface reading stale tab state. Ctrl+P could remain blocked behind “This tab is still starting…”, the sidebar could keep an old model or thinking level, and clicking a diff expander changed the underlying set without repainting the message.

v0.6.1 repairs that tab activation and reactivity work. It also adds last-request generation speed, keeps extension dialogs attached to their originating Pi process, and replaces the README mockups with captures rendered by the production application.

## The complete application

This is `src/index.tsx` running in tmux against a deterministic Pi RPC fixture. The transcript, thinking block, Bash/edit/subagent cards, supervisor notice, prompt, footer, and sidebar all come from production components.

![PiTTy conversation with tools and sidebar](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mistrjirka/PiTTy/v0.6.1/docs/screenshots/conversation.svg)

Ctrl+P opens over the same live conversation and keeps the surrounding session visible:

![PiTTy model selector](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mistrjirka/PiTTy/v0.6.1/docs/screenshots/model-selector.svg)

The captures can be regenerated with `bun run screenshots`; no screenshot-only UI component is involved.

## Why the initial tab said it was still starting

The boot process updated the global startup panel, but the new per-tab runtime never received the corresponding `startupResolved` state. The application looked ready while tab-scoped commands still saw `false`.

The boot runtime is now marked ready after state and history finish loading. Its asynchronous callbacks hold a reference to that runtime instead of resolving `activeRuntime()` later, so switching tabs during a slow startup cannot write the result into a different conversation.

## Every tab change now performs the same work

The first implementation had a correct `activateTab()` function, but three controls bypassed it:

- `+` changed `TabManager.activeId` directly;
- closing an active tab selected a fallback directly;
- Ctrl+Tab called `TabManager.cycle()` and repainted only the strip.

Those paths now converge on `activateTab()`. Each transition:

- restores the target tab's draft;
- resets its transcript window and scroll position;
- updates the extension-request owner;
- clears that tab's badge;
- repaints model, thinking, context, runs, and request speed;
- refreshes state and statistics once the runtime is ready.

Application shutdown now stops every live tab process. Closing one tab still stops only that tab.

## Sidebar values update with the selected Pi process

The tab runtime stores session state, statistics, subagent runs, expansion choices, and request performance in ordinary TypeScript objects. Solid cannot observe those mutations unless the getter also reads a signal. The affected accessors now subscribe to the shared revision signal, and their setters bump it after writing.

This fixes stale values for:

- provider and model ID;
- thinking level;
- context tokens, window, and percentage;
- session identity and streaming state;
- subagent runs and tools;
- per-request performance.

Background tabs continue to receive Pi events, but those events update only their runtime. Selecting the tab reveals its latest values.

State refreshes are single-flight per runtime rather than global. A delayed response from tab A therefore updates tab A even if tab B becomes active before the RPC finishes.

## Last-request latency and output speed

The sidebar can now show a line such as:

```text
TTFT 1.8s · 42 tok/s
```

`TTFT` is measured from the assistant request timestamp to the first text or thinking delta. `tok/s` uses Pi's final `usage.output` count divided by the time from that first delta to `message_end`. Pi includes reported reasoning tokens in `usage.output`.

The tracker stores the last successful model invocation per tab. It accepts normal `stop`, `toolUse`, and `length` completions and rejects overlapping, aborted, errored, zero-token, and out-of-order samples. If Pi does not provide enough information, the metric is absent; PiTTy does not display a zero or estimate prompt-processing throughput.

## Diff, tool, and thinking expansion

The click handlers were mutating per-tab sets and maps correctly, but the corresponding getters did not depend on a Solid signal. They now read the revision signal before consulting the active runtime.

- “Click to view diff” expands on the first click.
- Long tool output and thinking blocks follow the same rule.
- The expansion hint is hidden when the collapsed preview already contains all useful content.

Subagent tool cards were also tightened up. The header contains agent, model, mode, completion state, and elapsed time once. The task gist sits on its own line. Raw workflow JSON remains available through expansion rather than occupying the summary row.

## Extension dialogs belong to their originating tab

Extension UI requests now pass through a runtime-aware FIFO router.

- A request from the active tab is handled immediately.
- A request from a background tab increments its badge and waits.
- Switching to that tab opens the queue head.
- Switching away hides an interactive dialog without deleting it.
- The response is sent through the Pi client that created the dialog, not whichever tab happens to be active later.
- Closing a tab removes its queued requests.

Notifications, status/title updates, editor-prefill requests, and standard select/confirm/input/editor dialogs all use the same ownership path.

## CI is green on macOS again

The launcher fixture compared two equivalent macOS temporary paths as raw strings:

```text
/var/folders/…
/private/var/folders/…
```

Both sides are now resolved through `realpath()` before comparison. The fixture also clears inherited `PI_BIN` when it is testing bundled-Pi selection. This was the reason the main CI workflow was red while the Linux-only release workflow passed.

## Subagent handling validation

The focused rendering/subagent suite covers parallel child identity, active and completed ordering, models and thinking levels, tool activity, token/cost text, failure reasons, steering controls, supervisor messages, inspector actions, mission-backed children, and constrained layouts. The corrected tab routing keeps those updates isolated when their owner is in the background.

## Upgrade

```bash
pitty upgrade
```

Restart existing PiTTy processes after upgrading. Their running frontend code is not replaced in place.

## Verification

- TypeScript: clean
- Full suite: **354 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed** across 32 files
- Focused rendering + subagents: **150 passed**
- Screenshot generator: production app booted twice; conversation and model-selector state assertions passed
- Real-TUI smoke: created a second tab using the actual `+` target, waited for its Pi runtime, then opened Ctrl+P in that tab with no “still starting” notification
- Six-lane implementation review: logic, types, smell, architecture, reuse, and security completed; verified activation-path findings were fixed before release

## Known limits

Pi startup can still take roughly 90 seconds on the maintainer's current local setup when loading a large extension/session environment. PiTTy reports that as startup work instead of pretending the tab is ready. Request speed is omitted for providers or failed requests that do not expose a usable output count and timing sequence.
